    Gauge transformations preserve derivative surjectivity #

    Appendix A: "rescaling arrows and entire relations changes the mesh derivative by invertible diagonal maps, so it changes neither its cokernel nor the brick property." For c'_{x,a} = η_x c_{x,a} μ_{σ a} μ_a, the gauge functor kQ → kQ descends to a functor Φ : C(Q, c) → C(Q, c') with Φ(a) = μ_a a; and for f'_a = μ_a⁻¹ Φ(f_a), D'(f') = η Φ(D f). Hence each row of C(Q, c') lies in the image of D'_m when the corresponding row of C(Q, c) lies in that of D_m.

    References #

    • Multiplicative bases and deformations of representation-finite algebras, https://github.com/haruhisa-enomoto/multiplicative-bases-deformations. Numbered statements cited here refer to it.
